chapter: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
title: Lead trumpet with Wooding and giving up jazz
summary: He joined as lead trumpet because Bobby Martin could not do both jobs, stopped playing jazz for three years, and was caught up in the excitement of Europe.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh, very -- oh yes. Yes. I thought that was the greatest thing in the world, the band. I jumped in that band and I was playing lead trumpet. That's the thing that [were] very important, money. I joined Sam Wooding as a lead trumpet player because Bobby Martin was the lead trumpet player and also did the jazz thing and it was too much for him, so I just joined the band as the lead trumpet player and then I stopped playing jazz altogether.
It really broke my heart in a way but I was -- the excitement of being Europe with Sam Wooding was -- I just forgot about everything.
And I played this whole three years with Sam Wooding as lead trumpet player, all of his music and everything.
